To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TFIIB closes the polymerase active centre, positions the DNA template, assists in DNA opening, stimulates the catalytic step, prevents the emerging DNA-RNA hybrid from tilting and triggers TFIIB displacement.
TFIIB closes the polymerase active site, positions DNA and assists in its opening, binds the DNA template, stimulates the first catalytic steps, and prevents the emerging DNA-RNA hybrid from tilting.

TFIIB assists in DNA recruitment, induces binding of metal B and stimulates initial RNA formation allosterically, prevents the emerging DNA-RNA hybrid from tilting, and directs RNA to its exit tunnel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the transcription initiation process, and the role of the general transcription factor TFIIB.
the structure and function of RNA polymerase II, which is a key enzyme in gene expression and transcription regulation.
the molecular basis of the initiation of transcription, which is a central step of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B-reader loop of TFIIB is the first example of an allosteric RNA polymerase factor, and the first one that allosterically stimulates initial transcription.
TFIIB is a key factor that enables RNA polymerase to initiate transcription.

TFIIB is a transcription factor that assists in the recruitment of Pol II to DNA, in its opening, in the positioning of the transcription start site, in the binding and activation of the catalytic ion B, in the allosteric stimulation of the initial RNA synthesis and in the separation of the DNA and RNA products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TFIIB is an RNA polymerase ‘initiator’ and ‘primer separator’.

TFIIB functions as a molecular bridge that connects the transcription machinery to the DNA template and RNA product and that ensures their precise positioning and correct interactions during the initiation phase.
the B-reader of TFIIB functions as a molecular switch that controls the transition between initiation and elongation by regulating the access of DNA and RNA to the polymerase active site.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TFIIB is a key component of a sophisticated mechanism that ensures the correct initiation of transcription, and that TFIIB and the TFIIB-like proteins in other organisms have a similar function in the initiation of RNA synthesis.
the B-reader of TFIIB, which has been conserved for more than 2 billion years of evolution, plays a key role in the initiation of RNA transcription.
TFIIB is a multifunctional protein that controls all steps of RNA synthesis initiation.
